Mahesh N.P vs The United India Insurance Company Ltd on 10 March, 2025
Judgment

The petitioner in O.P.(MV) No. 535 of 2017 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Thalassery filed this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.

2. According to the petitioner, on 06.04.2017, while he was riding a motorcycle, car driven by the 2 nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner caused to hit the motorcycle and thereby, he fell down and sustained serious injuries.
The 1 st respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle and the 3rd respondent is the insurer.
3. Before the Tribunal, PWs 1 to 4 were examined and Exhibits A1 to A12 and X1 were marked from the side of the petitioner and no evidence was adduced from the side of the respondents.

4. The Tribunal recorded a finding that the accident occurred because of the negligence on the part of the 2 nd respondent and that respondents 1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation 2025:KER:19918 to the petitioner.

The Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.11,60,500/- to the petitioner.
5.

Heard Sri. M.V. Amaresan, the learned counsel for the appellant and Sri. A.A. Mohammed Nazir,
the learned counsel for the respondent insurance company.

6. The learned counsel for the appellant argued that the appellant was aged 36 years and earning Rs.27,000/- per month from his occupation as electrician and the Tribunal fixed only Rs.12,000/-
as notional income for the reason that no reliable evidence is adduced to prove the actual income.
7. The learned counsel for the appellant invited my attention to the evidence of PW2 and Exhibit A12 certificate issued by PW2 regarding the salary of the petitioner.

It is pointed out that the petitioner was examined as PW1 and he deposed that he was working as electrician under PW2 and earning a monthly salary of Rs.27,000/- and PW2 also deposed that the petitioner was working under him.

The learned counsel for the respondent insurance company pointed out that in cross examination,
PW2 admitted that he is not keeping a muster roll of the employees and he is also not maintaining any register in connection with the payment of salary.
The evidence of PW2 in cross examination indicates that the petitioner was working on daily wage basis.

9. A perusal of Exhibit A12 shows that the said letter was issued by PW2 only on 01.05.2019 and therefore, considering the evidence of PW2 in cross examination, I find no reason to disagree with Mahesh N.P vs The United India Insurance Company Ltd on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124097487/

sentences.text: the finding of the Tribunal that the evidence of PW2 and Exhibit A12 cannot be accepted as reliable evidence to prove the income of the petitioner.

10. The learned counsel for the appellant argued that the averment in the claim petition that the petitioner is a qualified electrician is not seriously disputed and in that circumstance, the notional income fixed by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

11. The learned counsel for the appellant relied on a notification bearing No. 56/2017 dated 28.04.2017 of the Finance Department 2025:KER:19918 regarding enhancement of wages of contract employees on daily wages.

It is pointed out that electricians come under category-II and as per the notification, the maximum daily wage payable in a month for the employees coming under category-II is Rs.18,450/-.
12.

But, it is pertinent to note that the said notification is not one issued as per the provisions of the Minimum Wages Act and the said notification is issued by the Finance Department for enhancement of wages of employees on daily wages and therefore, the same cannot be accepted as a minimum wage notification under the Minimum Wages Act.

However, considering the fact that the occurrence was in the year 2017 and the petitioner was a qualified electrician, I find that his notional income can be fixed as Rs.15,000/- per month for the purpose of calculating the compensation.

13. The learned counsel for the appellant invited my attention to Exhibit X1 disability certificate,
wherein the whole body permanent disability is assessed as 9% and permanent orthopedic disability as 30%.
The treatment records of the petitioner shows that he sustained crush injury left foot with fracture lateral malleolus.

2025:KER:19918 14. In Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar, (2011) 1 SCC 343], the Honourable Supreme Court summarised the principles for ascertainment of loss of earning capacity due to permanent disability as follows:
(i) All injuries (or permanent disabilities arising from injuries), do not result in loss of earning capacity.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar, (2011) 1 SCC 343]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (ii) The percentage of permanent disability with reference to the whole body of a person, cannot be assumed to be the percentage of loss of earning capacity.

To put it differently, the percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability (except in a few cases, where the Tribunal on the basis of evidence, concludes that the percentage of loss of earning capacity is the same as the percentage of permanent disability).

(iii) The doctor who treated an injured claimant or who examined him subsequently to assess the extent of his permanent disability can give evidence only in regard to the extent of permanent disability.
The loss of earning capacity is something that will have to be assessed by the Tribunal with reference to the evidence in entirety.

sentences.text:
(iv) The same permanent disability may result in different percentages of loss of earning capacity in different persons, depending upon the nature of profession,
occupation or job, age, education and other factors.
15. In this case, even though the whole body disability as per Exhibit X1 is only 9%, the Tribunal accepted 30% functional disability for calculating the compensation for loss of earning capacity.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries, physical disability assessed in X1 and occupation of the petitioner, I find no reason to interfere with the functional disability fixed by the Tribunal.
The learned counsel for the appellant pointed out that the Tribunal has not made any addition towards future prospects.

The decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd.
v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and Jagdish v. Mohan [(2018) 4 SCC 571] shows that the benefit of future prospects should not be confined only to those who have a permanent job and would extend to self-employed individuals and in case of a self-employed person, an addition of 40% of the established income should be made where the age of the victim at the time of the accident was below 40 years.
17. When the compensation for loss of earning capacity is calculated as per the revised criteria, the amount would come to Rs.11,34,000 [15000 + 40% x 12 x 15 x 30/100].

sentences.text: The Tribunal has already granted Rs.6,48,000/- under this head.
Therefore, an additional compensation of Rs.4,86,000/- is granted to the appellant under this head.
I find that the compensation granted by the Tribunal under other heads are reasonable and requires no interference.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to the enhanced compensation as given below:

Additional amount Compensation granted by Particulars awarded by the this Court Tribunal (Rs.) (Rs.) 4,86,000/-
 Loss of earning capacity 6,48,000/-

Total enhanced compensation  4,86,000/-
19.
Thus, a total amount of Rs.4,86,000/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Eighty Six Thousand only) is awarded as enhanced compensation.
The said amount shall carry interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of the application till realization.
The appellant would also be entitled to proportionate costs in the case.
The claimant shall furnish the details of the bank account to the insurance company for transfer of the amount.
